plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, coarse stem topped by a big flower head of golden ray florets surrounding a dark disc of tiny florets that mature into seeds. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky. It is widely cultivated for seed, oil and ornamental use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, the United States and Argentina
plants.funFact: Sunflower heads follow the sun only while young (heliotropism); mature flower heads typically stay facing east, which helps warm them in the morning and attract pollinators.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial herb that spreads by rhizomes and forms dense colonies. In late summer it produces arching plumes packed with tiny golden-yellow flower heads that are a magnet for bees, butterflies and other late-season pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to meadows, roadsides and prairies of eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often wrongly blamed for hay fever; its pollen is heavy and sticky and is carried by insects, while the real culprit is usually ragweed blooming at the same time.

plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: A low, evergreen, spreading shrub with tiny scale-like leaves and spikes of small bell-shaped flowers. It carpets moorlands and heaths in purple waves in late summer and is a key nectar source for bees, producing a prized dark heather honey.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (July to October)
plants.location: Moorlands, heaths and acidic soils of Scotland, Ireland, Scandinavia and northern Europe; naturalized in parts of North America
plants.funFact: Heather was historically used to make beds, thatch roofs, brooms, rope and even ale, and the Scottish tradition holds that white heather brings good luck.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody evergreen shrub of the fynbos with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, up to 30 cm across. The showy, bowl-shaped head is made of colorful bracts surrounding a center of many small flowers, and it is South Africa's national flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering from August to November and some blooms in late summer
plants.location: Southwestern and southern coastal regions of South Africa, in the Cape Floristic Region
plants.funFact: Proteas are among the oldest flowering plants, dating back around 300 million years to when the continents were joined as Gondwana, and they are adapted to fire, resprouting from underground lignotubers.
